column1: zsh vs bash: does an UNQUOTED expansion ($var, $*, $@) get word-split?
column2:
bash: YES — splits every unquoted expansion on IFS (space/tab/newline).
zsh:  NO  — for PARAMETER expansion: unquoted $var / $* / $@ stay intact.

  for a in $*; ...   with args: apple "two words" peal
    zsh  -> apple | "two words" | peal   (3 words)
    bash -> apple | two | words | peal     (4 words)

So swapping $* for $@ in zsh changes nothing, and a spaced filename survives
unquoted. Split on purpose with ${=var} / ${(s:X:)var}.
(Exception: command substitution $(...) DOES split in zsh — see asymmetry card.)

column1: zsh: how do you force-split a string into words?
column2:
str="two words"
${=str}        # = flag  -> IFS word-split (like bash would)
${(s: :)str}   # (s:SEP:) -> split on a specific separator (a space here)
${(s:,:)csv}   # e.g. split CSV on commas

IFS = Internal Field Separator (default: space, tab, newline).
(setopt shwordsplit makes zsh split everywhere like bash — avoid; too surprising.)

column1: zsh: does UNQUOTED command substitution $(cmd) split? (vs a plain $var)
column2:
Asymmetry (SH_WORD_SPLIT off = default):
  $var  $*  $@    PARAMETER expansion    -> NOT split (stays one value)
  $(cmd)  `cmd`    COMMAND substitution   -> SPLIT on IFS
  "$(cmd)"         quoted                 -> one word

bash splits BOTH forms; zsh splits only command-sub / backticks.
  for w in $(echo 'a b c'); ...  -> a | b | c   (yes, even in zsh)
